=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py
Line or code reference: lines 883-898 (_cached_row_needs_cancelled_failure_point_backfill) with the changed precedence at lines 915-923
Problem: The cancelled-run cache backfill predicate only re-fetches a cached cancelled row when its cached failure_point has neither job_name nor step_name, and it immediately returns False when run_id is already in cancelled_jobs_seen_lookup. The last-run change now makes compute_run_metrics prefer the cancellation location for a cancelled run, so cached rows produced by the previous iteration of this branch can have a non-empty failure_point that still carries the old failure-first attribution. Those rows are skipped forever because run_id is already in cancelled_jobs_seen_lookup and the non-empty failure_point suppresses refetch.
Why it fails at runtime: When the collector reads an existing workflow_log_analysis_cache containing such a cancelled run, main reuses the stale row without calling list_jobs_for_run. The report therefore keeps mis-attributing the run to a failure job/step instead of the actual cancellation job/step, which is the precise observability defect issue 3753 requires eliminating.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- File: scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py
Line or code reference: compute_run_metrics() (lines 913-919) — the fallback chain
Problem: For a cancelled run that also has a failed job or failed step, the fallback `failure_point = extract_failure_point(jobs)` replaces the cancellation-specific point with the failure location. The linked issue (#3753) says to surface where cancellation happened for cancelled runs as "best-effort", and the `_extract_cancelled_point` function already returns cancellation evidence when present. The fallback overwrites that evidence whenever the cancelled run also carries failure evidence — so a run that was cancelled mid-flight after another job had already failed will report the failure location instead of the cancellation point, defeating the observability purpose for mixed-signal cancelled runs.
Why it fails at runtime: A run with conclusion "cancelled" that includes a separate failed job (e.g. lint failed, validate was cancelled) will have its `failure_point` report the lint failure step rather than where cancellation happened, so downstream consumers cannot distinguish "cancelled at X" from "cancelled but another job failed at Y".
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- File: scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py
Line or code reference: _cached_row_needs_cancelled_failure_point_backfill() (lines 881-897)
Problem: The backfill guard only triggers when the cached `failure_point` has neither `job_name` nor `step_name` (both falsy). If a cached cancelled row has a stale/partial `failure_point` from before this PR (e.g. a `failure_point` that was backfilled from failure evidence but not cancellation evidence), it will NOT be re-fetched because `failure_point.get("job_name")` is truthy. Old cached cancelled rows with partial failure-only `failure_point` data remain locationless with respect to cancellation.
Why it fails at runtime: Cached cancelled runs from prior invocations that had a failure-point but no cancellation-point will keep reusing that stale row instead of fetching jobs to compute `_extract_cancelled_point`. The `cancelled_jobs_seen_set` only prevents re-fetching runs that were already processed by this new code path, but old cache rows that already had a `failure_point` with a truthy job_name from a prior failure-only collection pass are never backfilled.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

Requirement: "Cancelled pre-step or queue-only runs are no longer locationless in collector output when job data provides a clue." (Acceptance criterion #1 from issue #3753)
Expected change site: scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py — compute_run_metrics() and the fallback logic
Evidence of absence: For cancelled runs with mixed signals (both failure and cancellation present), the fallback `failure_point = extract_failure_point(jobs)` at line 919 overwrites the cancellation point with the failure point, so the cancellation location is lost when failure evidence exists alongside cancellation evidence. The test `test_compute_run_metrics_cancelled_step_precedence_then_job_fallback` only asserts the happy path where cancellation wins (no competing failure step in the validate job), but does not cover the case where a cancelled run also has a separate failed job/step that would win via the fallback.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- File: scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py:873-880 (compute_run_metrics)
Line or code reference: `if normalized_conclusion == "failure": failure_point = extract_failure_point(jobs) elif normalized_conclusion == "cancelled": failure_point = _extract_cancelled_point(jobs); if not (failure_point.get("job_name") or failure_point.get("step_name")): failure_point = extract_failure_point(jobs)`
Problem: When a cancelled run also has a failure step/job (common GitHub behaviour when cancellation occurs after a step failure), the failure location is returned instead of the cancellation clue.
Why it fails at runtime: The linked issue requires the cancellation point to surface ("where cancellation happened"). The test `test_compute_run_metrics_cancelled_step_precedence_then_job_fallback` asserts the opposite ordering but the production path prefers failure first, so cancelled runs remain mis-attributed.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- File: scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py:1528-1535 (main cache guard)
Line or code reference: `needs_cancelled_backfill = _cached_row_needs_cancelled_failure_point_backfill(...) if ... and not needs_cancelled_backfill: reuse cached row` + `_cached_row_needs_cancelled_failure_point_backfill` (lines 885-897)
Problem: The guard only forces a re-fetch when the cached `failure_point` is completely empty. A stale partial point (e.g. `{"job_name": "foo"}` but no `step_name`) satisfies the `if not (job_name or step_name)` check and is reused. The `cancelled_jobs_seen_set` update only occurs on the fresh path.
Why it fails at runtime: Old cache entries for cancelled runs can stay locationless after the collector change, defeating the backfill intent. The test that exercises the refetch path only hits the fully-empty case.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
